messages:
sam: Hey team — incoming customer report: multiple 503s for hosted inference over a ~45s window. They send a burst of 20 concurrent generate+embed requests. SDK shows retries & backoff piling up; customer noticed a surprise billing spike. attaching logs (redacted).

maria: got it. any correlation with deployments or infra changes?

sam: customer says this started yesterday afternoon, no deploys on our side at the same time. timestamps: 2026-03-12T15:03:05Z -> 15:03:50Z.

jonathan: can you paste the request headers example and auth flow? curious if token refresh fan-out is involved.

sam: headers snippet attached inline: 
```
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
User-Agent: RedwoodSDK/1.4.0
X-Request-Id: abc123
```
They use a short-lived token with client-side auto-refresh.

ryan: quick note — we shipped an experimental session-coalescing optimization in edge proxy late Feb to reduce auth refresh storms. It groups concurrent sessions to reuse upstream connections; could introduce brief contention under aligned refreshes.

lucy: interesting — coalescing should reduce connections, not 503s, but I can see a path: if coalescing serializes some auth validation and an upstream times out, it could return 5xx for the whole group.

maria: can we repro? steps to try: ask the customer to run a small script that issues 20 parallel requests with token expiring in 30s, and enable SDK debug logs. if we can reproduce we can toggle coalescing for their tenant.

sam: proposed repro script (python):
```
# loop spawning 20 threads calling /v1/generate
# set token TTL=30s
for i in range(20):
    spawn_request()
```
I'll share exact script.

supportbot: Incident created: INC-2026-0312-503-COALESCE, owner @maria, severity P2.

jonathan: while we get repro, short mitigation: ask customer to set env var REDWOOD_SESSION_COALESCE=false in their SDK config to disable coalescing client-side (we rolled a flag that also respects client hint). That should avoid grouped auth validation. Also suggest increasing auth token TTL if possible.

sam: customer rolled the flag and re-ran. initial result: fewer 503s, but still occasional 502s at peak.

lucy: can you grab proxy logs for their tenant for the timeframe? look for connection pooling errors, upstream timeouts, and our coalescing debug traces.

ryan: pulled logs. we see a pattern: when 12+ concurrent refreshes hit exactly when a stale upstream TLS session is pruned, connection setup to upstream auth service spikes latency -> some requests exceed proxy connect timeout (1.5s) -> 503 returned. There are also short bursts of retry loops from the SDK.

maria: root cause hypothesis: session coalescing reduces overall connections but creates brief synchronized windows where many requests wait on a single connection slot; if the upstream TLS handshake or auth service is slow, queued requests hit gateway timeouts.

sam: status for customer: "We're investigating a synchronization edge in session coalescing that can cause transient 5xx when many clients refresh at the same aligned TTL. Temporary mitigation: disable session coalescing in your SDK and/or increase token TTL. We will provide a fix and config to reduce serialization."

jonathan: engineering action items:
- add guard to coalescing code to fail-open faster (200ms) and allow fallback to new connection when queue grows
- instrument queue length metric and add alert on >8 waiting refreshes
- consider jitter on client-side refresh windows to avoid alignment

ryan: quick patch landed to proxy: if queue_wait_ms > 150 then spawn new connection instead of waiting. deploying to canary now (edge-candidate slot).

supportbot: Deploy started: edge-proxy v2.7.4-canary at 2026-03-12T17:01:10Z.

maria: ping customer after canary: ask them to re-run repro with coalescing on and with debug logs. we'll monitor.

sam: customer ran canary test at 17:10. results: 0 503s in 30 tests, previous baseline had ~6/30. customer confirms billing anomaly reduced.

lucy: rolling the patch to stable region in next 30m. also adding config toggle at tenant-level to disable coalescing server-side if needed.

maria: communications: I'll update the customer thread and note that a fix is deployed to canary and we expect full roll in 30m, asking them to re-open if they still see issues.

sam: thanks all. follow-ups: add a KB article recommending token TTL guidelines and sample jitter code for SDKs.

supportbot: Incident INC-2026-0312-503-COALESCE marked monitoring at 2026-03-12T17:45:20Z.
